data.one_liner: Model-driven form handling and validation inspired by Angular Reactive Forms
data.what_it_does: Separates form data models and validation logic from UI widgets using FormGroups, FormArrays, and FormControls. It provides built-in sync and async validators, custom validation hooks, and specialized widgets that bind directly to reactive controls. It tracks validity, touched status, and enabled states across nested form structures.
use_when: Building complex forms with inter-dependent field validations like password matching
Managing dynamic form structures like arrays or groups of inputs that grow at runtime
Needing fine-grained control over validation timing, asynchronous checks, or error message display
avoid_when: The application only requires a few basic text inputs where standard Flutter Form and TextFormField suffice
You prefer pure immutable functional form modeling without Angular-style control objects
strengths: Rich set of pre-built validators, cross-field validation, and async validator support with debounce
Comprehensive suite of dedicated reactive widgets (text fields, checkboxes, pickers)
Clean separation of form state and business logic from the widget tree
weaknesses: Steep learning curve if not already familiar with Angular's reactive form concepts
Requires high minimum Flutter SDK version (>=3.29.0) for the latest release
data.setup_notes: May require intl dependency override if version conflicts occur.

alternatives.name: formz
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose formz for a lightweight, immutable, functional approach often paired with Bloc instead of model-driven control trees.
